hook.line: The lawyer arrives tomorrow and Tomás and Vale are still working out who does what. Plans like this need one small phrase: the one that says we settled it.
hook.es: Quedamos en vernos a las ocho en el café.
hook.en: We agreed to meet at eight at the café.

examples.es: Quedamos en vernos a las ocho en el café.
examples.en: We agreed to meet at eight at the café.

examples.es: Quedamos en que tú traías la torta.
examples.en: We agreed that you'd bring the cake. (to a friend)

examples.es: Quedaron en llamar a la abogada mañana.
examples.en: They agreed to call the lawyer tomorrow.

examples.es: Quedamos en que yo cocino y tú lavas los platos.
examples.en: We agreed that I cook and you wash the dishes. (to a friend)
We didn't agree on any time.

rule:
*Quedar en* is how two people say they settled a plan. After it comes either the dictionary form (*quedamos en vernos*) or *que* plus a full sentence (*quedamos en que yo cocino*).

English says *agreed to* or *agreed on*. Spanish says *en* every time. It is nearly always *we* or *they*, because it takes two people to agree.

*¿En qué quedamos?* is what you say when things have got fuzzy: so what did we decide?

Don't mix it up with *quedarse*, which means to stay.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a fixed verb plus preposition. *Quedar* alone means to be left or to arrange, so the *en* is what points to the agreement.

readAndPick.es: Quedamos en vernos a las ocho.
options: We agreed to meet at eight.
We stayed to see each other at eight.
We saw each other at eight.

readAndPick.es: Quedaron en llamar a la abogada.
options: We agreed to call the lawyer.
They stayed to call the lawyer.
They agreed to call the lawyer.
What are we staying in?
So what did we decide?
Where are we meeting?

readAndPick.es: Quedamos en que tú traías la torta.
options: We agreed that you'd bring the cake.
We agreed that I'd bring the cake.
You stayed to bring the cake.

readAndPick.es: Quedamos en que yo traía la torta.
options: We agreed that you'd bring the cake.
We agreed that I'd bring the cake.
We stayed no hours.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *en* or *a* and type the whole sentence: Quedamos ___ vernos a las ocho en el café. (We agreed to meet at eight at the café.)
yourTurn.answer: Quedamos en vernos a las ocho en el café.
yourTurn.why: Agreeing on a plan takes *en*, not *a* or *de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: We agreed to talk later.
yourTurn.why: *Quedamos en* plus the dictionary form says what you settled on.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: They agreed to call the lawyer tomorrow.
yourTurn.answer: Quedaron en llamar a la abogada mañana.
accept: Quedaron en llamar mañana a la abogada.
yourTurn.why: *They* is *quedaron*. The verb after *en* stays in its dictionary form.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: So what did we decide?
yourTurn.why: The question word *qué* comes right after *en*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend: We agreed that I cook and you wash the dishes.
yourTurn.answer: Quedamos en que yo cocino y tú lavas los platos.
accept: Quedamos en que cocino yo y lavas tú los platos.
yourTurn.why: With a full sentence after the plan, use *en que* and keep both verbs in the plain present.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Quedamos en hablar después.* (We didn't agree to talk later.)
yourTurn.why: Put *no* in front of *quedamos*. Everything else stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it into a question for a friend: *Quedamos en ir juntos.* (Did we agree to go together?)
yourTurn.why: The words stay the same. Only the question marks and your voice change.

pitfalls.wrong: Quedamos a vernos a las ocho.
pitfalls.right: Quedamos en vernos a las ocho.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says agreed to, but here Spanish uses *en*.

pitfalls.wrong: Nos quedamos en vernos a las ocho.
pitfalls.right: Quedamos en vernos a las ocho.
pitfalls.why: *Quedarse* means to stay. To agree on a plan, use plain *quedar*, with no *nos* in front.

pitfalls.wrong: Quedamos que tú traías la torta.
pitfalls.right: Quedamos en que tú traías la torta.
pitfalls.why: The *en* stays in front of *que*, even though English drops it.

personal: Think of a plan you agreed with someone this week and say it with *quedamos en*.
